name: Should I use interior chinking or clear sealant between my logs?

mainEntity.name: Should I use interior chinking or clear sealant between my logs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Chinking is typically necessary for wider joint lines (often a half-inch wide or larger) and classic stacked-log designs, while clear sealants or caulking handle tighter seams, tongue-and-groove joints, and upward-facing checks. Chinking contains aggregate that gives it a traditional textured appearance and high elasticity to stretch as logs shift. Smooth caulks or clear finishes provide a clean, modern aesthetic but are formulated for narrower joints. Choosing between them involves a practical tradeoff between maintaining a rustic, historic appearance or achieving a streamlined, contemporary finish that blends cleanly with drywall or finished trim.
acceptedAnswer.description: Use chinking for wider, shifting gaps and a traditional textured look; use clear sealers or smooth elastomeric caulks for narrow seams and tight checks.
